title: GammaCare POC kickoff — success guardrails and deployment proposal
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures our kickoff notes, proposed deployment approach, and explicit success guardrails for GammaCare's 8-week POC. GammaCare is a mid-stage healthtech providing clinician-facing triage and summarization features; they require PHI protections and low-latency multi-turn chat over patient notes.

Quick summary / ask:
- POC goal: validate a Private (VPC) Redwood deployment that can serve a clinician assistant for triage + summarization with acceptable latency and clear cost estimates.
- Deliverables: working Private deployment (sandbox VPC), integration adapter to their EHR test dataset, automated eval harness (1000 test prompts), load test report, and a short runbook for handover.
- Timeline: 8 weeks from kickoff (integration + baseline -> iterate -> final acceptance).

Background/context (from pre-kickoff calls):
- GammaCare needs HIPAA-equivalent controls (audit logs, KMS integration). They prefer on-cloud VPC rather than on-prem for this POC.
- Target user is clinician triage team: quick summarization of visit notes and extraction of red-flag items.
- Expected traffic during POC: 20–40 concurrent clinicians, peak synthetic load for test at 80 QPS.

Scope (in-scope for POC):
- Private deployment (customer VPC) using Redwood Private control plane with customer-managed networking.
- Integrate with sample EHR exports (deidentified) provided by GammaCare test environment.
- Implement a reference prompt flow: context window + conversation memory + KV cache.
- Simple front-end demo (React) to exercise flows; not production UI.
- Basic observability: per-route latency and token cost dashboard, error traces, and a small set of eval prompts.

Out-of-scope:
- Full production data migration, deep EHR connector work, custom model training, or long-term SLA/contract negotiation.

Acceptance / success criteria (explicit, measurable) — both engineering and product: 
1) Functional correctness (product):
   - Summaries: average human-rated relevance >= 4/5 on a 100-sample blind eval (internal clinicians).
   - Information fidelity (hallucination rate on key facts) <= 7% on targeted extraction tests.
2) Performance (SRE/infra):
   - Latency: p95 end-to-end response time <= 350ms for single-turn summarization flows at expected concurrency (20–40). Note: multi-turn chat can be higher; define p95 <= 450ms for typical 3-turn flows.
   - Throughput: system must sustain a 80 QPS synthetic load for 5 minutes during load test without request failures > 0.5%.
3) Cost and economics (product + customer):
   - Token cost estimate delivered for steady-state load; target incremental cost per 1000 summarization requests <= $X (TBD based on quant/packing). Aim to present two configs: latency-optimized (higher cost) and cost-optimized (quantized).
4) Security & compliance (legal/security):
   - KMS integrated for data-at-rest keys (customer-managed).
   - Audit logs exported to their SIEM (sample events for 30 days retention in POC sandbox).
5) Operational handoff:
   - Runbook + one-page rollback and fallback policy documented.
   - Canary deploy and automatic fallback to smaller model variant tested during rollout demo.

Acceptance tests (how we'll measure the above):
- Run the 1000-prompt evaluation harness; collect human scores on 100-sample subset.
- Synthetic load script (k6 or locust) to hit 80 QPS for 5 minutes; measure p95/p99 and error rate.
- Simulate KMS rotation; verify audit trail and that tokens remain decryptable.
- Verify fallback policy by intentionally exhausting capacity of the primary pool and confirm automatic routing to fallback variant within 60s.

Proposed technical approach / deployment plan:
Week 0 (prep): sign access matrix, get GammaCare test VPC peering details, confirm KMS ARNs, collect sample EHR exports (deidentified), and open JIRA backlog.
Week 1–2 (baseline deploy): provision Redwood Private sandbox in GammaCare VPC (small instance pool), baseline model (open LlamaX small / Redwood-verified baseline) deployed, basic demo UI, wiring of audit logs.
Week 3–4 (integration + eval): integrate prompt templates, implement prefix/KV caching, run initial functional eval, iterate prompts.
Week 5 (load + resilience): run load tests, test autoscaling and fallback policies, measure latencies and cost.
Week 6–7 (polish + runbook): address gaps, freeze POC config, handover runbook and cost model, customer walkthrough.
Week 8 (acceptance): deliver final report, collect acceptance sign-off or list of follow-ups.

Key design choices and rationale (tradeoffs):
- Private vs Dedicated: Private chosen because of KMS/PHI needs and their preference for VPC control. Dedicated would reduce operator friction but not provide the same tenant-level KMS isolation.
- Model variants: start with mid-size open model (quant-friendly) that we can run with 8-bit quant to keep cost predictable. For latency-critical flows, suggest a CPU+GPU hybrid route for embedding-heavy lookups.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for multi-turn sessions to reduce per-token cost; expected token cost savings 20–30% on conversation-heavy workflows.

Roles & responsibilities (GammaCare vs Redwood):
- GammaCare: provide test VPC peering info, KMS ARNs, deidentified EHR samples, sign any sandbox access docs, designate 1 product and 1 security contact.
- Redwood SE (Alyssa): POC lead, infra provisioning, runbook owner.
- Redwood Eng (Diego): Private deployment, networking, KMS wiring.
- Redwood ML (Priya): prompt engineering, eval harness, quality measurement.
- Redwood SRE (Samir): load testing, autoscaling config, rollback policy.

Open questions / risks (items to resolve quickly):
- Q: Exact cost target per 1000 summarizations — GammaCare to provide target budget or we propose two profiles.
- Risk: Customer's EHR export format variant may require additional parsing; ask for a sample ASAP.
- Risk: KMS policy/coarse permissions could delay wiring; need security contacts looped in Week 0.

Kickoff agenda (30–45m recommended):
1) Introductions & objectives (5m)
2) POC scope and deliverables (10m)
3) Success criteria walk-through (10m)
4) Technical approach and network/KMS checklist (10m)
5) Next steps & immediate actions (5m)

Immediate next actions (before Week 0 ends):
- GammaCare to share deidentified sample EHR file (format examples) and KMS details — owner: GammaCare infra (due in 3 business days).
- Redwood to create JIRA-SE-4123 epic and rough backlog (Alyssa) and share skeleton Confluence page for acceptance metrics (link in linked_artifacts).
- Schedule deep-dive session on network peering with GammaCare infra (Diego).

Notes-to-self / SE working reminders (informal):
- Bring up fallback demo using a smaller open model (LLAMA-m45-like) to show graceful degradation.
- Prepare two cost-configs: one quantized low-cost path and one latency-optimized path (unquantized or fp16).
- Add a checklist item to test KV cache correctness for multi-turn summaries (memory + redaction sanity).

Appendix: quick measurement definitions (so acceptance is unambiguous)
- p95 latency: 95th percentile of end-to-end request time measured at Redwood ingress (includes model runtime + network inside VPC).
- Hallucination rate: % of evaluated outputs where a human annotator marks 1+ fabricated fact in required fields.
- Throughput sustainment: percentage of requests served during the synthetic 80 QPS window with status 200.
